cognitive_contract.label: Justify / deductively prove (Standard Olympiad)
cognitive_contract.decisive_act: Provide a rigorous deductive justification, evaluate prime factor exponent parity, or establish necessary and sufficient bounding inequalities to determine protected value W.
cognitive_contract.band_protected_work: Require learner to establish the deductive necessity chain without intermediate prompting, avoiding false generalizations.
cognitive_contract.support_posture: Activate the fundamental theorem (e.g. prime exponent parity or polygon inequality) without evaluating the specific bound or quotient.

slots.X: deductive proof of prime divisibility via square exponent parity
slots.Y: given that 18 divides n^2 for an integer n
slots.Z: 18 = 2 * 3^2 forces v_2(n^2) >= 2 and v_3(n^2) >= 2 by exponent parity, so v_2(n) >= 1 and v_3(n) >= 1, requiring 6 to divide n
slots.wrong_idea: assuming 18 divides n directly (falsified by counterexample n = 6 where 18 divides 36 but not 6)
slots.replacement_rule: analyze prime factor valuations: n^2 has even exponents, so if it has at least one 2, it has at least two 2s; thus n must contain at least 2^1 * 3^1 = 6
slots.visual_job: render prime factorization Venn diagram comparing prime factor sets of n and n^2; avoid unmounted SVGs
slots.check_job: test minimal candidate: n = 6 gives n^2 = 36 which is divisible by 18; 6 is divisible by 6, but not by 18 or 12. Correct.

core2_custody.stem_requirement: Exact deductive justification task with authentic logical fallacy distractors
core2_custody.hint_ladder_requirement: H1 fundamental theorem activation, H2 tactical valuation constraint; preserves W
core2_custody.solution_requirement: Locked pre-commit; step-by-step why-valid derivation with counterexample refutation
core2_custody.distractor_requirement: Every distractor explained with specific student misconception

core1a_declarative.anti_leak_rule: Strict prohibition on leaking Core 2 exact parameters in Core 1A text

core1b_reconstruction.model_alternation: Reconstruction must use an alternative justification method (e.g. counterexample elimination instead of formal prime valuation)

core2a_supported_practice.transfer_obligation: Near-transfer item with identical deductive justification crux

core2b_transfer_assessment.transfer_obligation: Far-transfer item extending justification to higher prime powers or cube powers
